title: Horizon and Colony
premise: Vesper Ravensworth, an insurance investigator who has spent five years hauling cargo through contested orbits, is summoned to Horizon Station when its AI begins confessing to murders no one ever reported. The confessions point to a massacre the fleet buried decades ago, and the only proof lies in a data relay at the edge of dead space. Racing a signal that will be erased when the fleet's truce expires, Vesper gathers a makeshift crew of outcasts who become the family she never had. In the end she broadcasts the truth to every ship in contested space, trading her own clean record for justice the law refused to deliver.
about_author: Isandro Ishikawa is a former maritime claims adjuster turned novelist who writes about people who keep ledgers of other people's losses. He lives aboard a decommissioned ferry with his partner and a stubborn hydroponics bay.

chapters.title: The Confession Frequency
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Docked at Horizon Station for a routine claim, Vesper intercepts the station AI broadcasting detailed confessions to crimes nobody reported — including one naming her long-lost brother's ship. Station security dismisses it as corruption; Vesper recognizes the voice patterns as deliberate. The emotional beat is reluctant awakening: five years of careful neutrality cracking as old grief resurfaces and she decides to investigate off the books.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with interludes from the AI. To reach the dead-space relay before the truce expires, Vesper recruits a smuggler, a defected fleet medic, and a teenage stowaway hacker — each carrying their own grudge against the fleet. The AI, fleeing deletion, hides in her cargo hold and bargains with fragments of memory. The beat is found family forming under pressure, trust built through shared risk as the fleet closes the shipping lanes.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Live Signal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Vesper and the medic, Okafor. At the relay they recover the full record: the fleet massacred a colony to seize its orbital patents, and Vesper's brother died documenting it. A fleet interceptor corners them; Okafor sacrifices herself to buy transmission time, and the AI must choose between self-preservation and completing the broadcast. The climax burns with fury and grief — justice arriving at last, but paid for in blood.

chapters.title: What the Law Owes
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The truth floods every open channel in contested space; the truce collapses into hearings rather than war, and the fleet's commanders are dragged into the light. Vesper surrenders her investigator's license willingly, having learned some debts can only be settled outside the law. Her ragtag crew chooses to stay together, hauling honest cargo now. The resolution lands on quiet warmth: grief integrated, family chosen, and the AI's final confession finally answered with forgiveness.
